# Glossary · Sözlük (EN ↔ TR) {#sec-glossary}

A running bilingual glossary, grouped by topic and alphabetized within each
group. Terms marked ◆ are conventionally left in English in Turkish
technical writing; a Turkish gloss is given where a usable one exists, and
proper nouns and metric names are left as they are. This
table is also the terminology contract between the two editions: both
pages are generated from the same `glossary.csv`, so edit there first and
translate second.

## Agents

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| agent loop | ajan döngüsü | a while-loop around a model with tools: the model chooses an action, the runtime executes it, the result is appended, repeat until the model stops calling tools |
| code mode | kod kipi | the model writes code, run in a sandbox, that calls the tools instead of calling them one at a time; at the extreme a general interpreter replaces the tool list, trading a readable allowlist for composability |
| compaction | sıkıştırma | summarising or dropping parts of an agent's transcript so the context stops growing; lossy, and you choose the loss before knowing what will be needed |
| context isolation | bağlam yalıtımı | running a read-heavy sub-task in its own window and returning only its conclusion, so the parent's context never carries what it read — the reading is still paid for, by the sub-agent |
| dead-letter queue | dead-letter queue ◆ | where a task that keeps failing lands so a person reads it, instead of retrying forever or vanishing |
| effective context length | etkin bağlam uzunluğu | the length at which a model still performs, as opposed to the length it accepts; routinely far shorter than the advertised window |
| guardrail | korkuluk | a runtime check that reduces accidental harm; not a security boundary, which is @sec-agent-security's distinction |
| handoff | handoff ◆ | a coordinator passes the conversation itself to another agent, which now owns it; unlike delegation, nothing is left to summarise or reject what the second agent does |
| idempotency | idempotency ◆ | a call that can be repeated without repeating its effect; what makes a retried agent step safe |
| parallel tool calling | paralel araç çağırma | a model emitting several tool calls in one turn, which collapses many loop iterations into one and is often one of the largest levers on agent cost when the calls are independent |
| progressive disclosure | kademeli açılım | loading only the tool definitions relevant to a step instead of all of them, so a large tool surface does not tax every call |
| prompt injection | prompt enjeksiyonu | instructions planted in content the model reads, which it cannot distinguish from your own |
| step cap | adım bütçesi | the maximum number of loop iterations; not a tuning parameter but an admission that the loop's exit is a model decision and may never be taken |
| tool call | araç çağrısı | a structured request the model emits — a function name and arguments — which the runtime, not the model, decides whether to execute |
| tool schema | araç şeması | the name, description, types and enums a model sees; prompt text rather than documentation, because the model gets one shot from it and cannot check a guess |
| trajectory | trajectory ◆ | the sequence of decisions, tool calls, observations and retries that led an agent to its answer; two runs can share the answer and differ in the trajectory |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Annotation and data quality

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| adjudication | uzlaştırma | a third pass that settles disagreements between two annotators |
| annotation guideline | etiketleme kılavuzu | the written rules that make labels reproducible by someone else |
| class imbalance | sınıf dengesizliği | one label dominates, so accuracy has to be read against the majority-class baseline |
| Cohen's kappa | Cohen kappa ◆ | agreement corrected for how much chance alone would produce |
| deduplication | tekilleştirme | removing near-identical documents; *yinelenen ayıklama* also seen |
| gold standard | altın standart | the labels treated as correct when scoring a model |
| ground truth | referans etiketler | the labels treated as correct when scoring; manufactured by people and processes, not discovered |
| inter-annotator agreement (IAA) | etiketleyiciler arası uyum | how often two annotators independently pick the same label |
| label leakage | etiket sızıntısı | a feature that encodes the answer; inflates scores until deployment |
| label noise | etiket gürültüsü | labels that disagree with the text they describe; concentrates at the top of a confidence-sorted error list |
| model card | model kartı | the short document stating what a model was trained on and where not to use it |
| out-of-fold prediction | out-of-fold kestirim ◆ | each training row is predicted by a model that never saw it, so confident disagreements flag labels worth reading |
| provenance | provenance ◆ | where a record came from and when: source, date, licence, the event that produced it and how confident the extractor was |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Decoding and structured output

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| abstention | çekimserlik | refusing to answer when confidence is low, so the answers you do give are more reliable; needs a score to threshold on |
| constrained decoding | kısıtlı kod çözme | masking the logits at each step to the tokens a grammar allows, so invalid output becomes unreachable rather than unlikely |
| decoding | kod çözme | turning the model's per-step scores into actual tokens; *çözümleme* would be *analysis*, a different operation |
| logprob | log olasılık | the log probability the model assigned to a token; the cheapest confidence signal available. Cleanest when the answer is one token — over several tokens the conditional log probabilities add, and sums over different lengths or tokenizations are defined but not comparable at face value |
| min-p | min-p ◆ | a cutoff scaled to the top token's probability rather than to a fixed mass, so it adapts to how peaked the distribution is |
| structured output | yapılandırılmış çıktı | output constrained to a schema rather than merely requested in prose |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Evaluation

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| benchmark contamination | benchmark bulaşması | test items that were in a model's training data, so the score reports memorisation rather than capability |
| position bias | konum yanlılığı | a judge preferring whichever slot a candidate sits in (first or second, depending on the model); measured by running the same comparison in both orders and counting the flips |
| statistical power | istatistiksel güç | the probability that an evaluation detects a real difference of a given size; what decides how many items an eval set needs |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Evaluation and serving

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| average precision (AP) | ortalama kesinlik (AP) ◆ | a weighted mean of precision at each threshold where recall increases; a summary of the precision-recall curve rather than its trapezoidal area, and unlike AUC it moves with the class balance, so quote the base rate beside it |
| base rate | taban oran | the share of a corpus that belongs to a given class; for the largest class it is also the accuracy of always guessing it |
| benchmark | kıyaslama ◆ | *benchmark* dominant |
| bias (in a model or corpus) | yanlılık | not *önyargı*, which is the psychological sense |
| Brier score | Brier skoru ◆ | mean squared error of a predicted probability; rewards a model for being right *and* honest about it |
| calibration | kalibrasyon | whether a score of 0.8 really means "right about 80% of the time"; a separate property from accuracy |
| cascade | cascade ◆ | answer with a cheap model and escalate only when a validator rejects the answer |
| checksum | sağlama toplamı | check digits that make a mistyped identifier detectable; which errors are caught depends on the scheme — the TCKN checksum in the guardrails chapter catches every single-digit error, and not every scheme does |
| confusion matrix | karışıklık matrisi | for a binary classifier, the four counts — TP, FP, FN, TN — that the usual metrics are computed from; with K classes it is a K×K table |
| continuous batching | sürekli batchleme ◆ | new requests join a running batch as slots free, instead of waiting for the whole batch to finish; the throughput lever in every modern server |
| decision threshold | karar eşiği | the cut that turns a score into a label; a free parameter you choose on held-out data, not a property of the model |
| drift | kayma | a metric moving while your code did not: the model behind the API changed, the inputs moved, or the surrounding system changed — three causes that look identical on a dashboard. *Input drift* is the second |
| escalation | aktarma | sending a request the cheap path could not handle to a stronger model or a person; its rate sets what a cascade costs |
| evaluation | değerlendirme | |
| expected calibration error (ECE) | beklenen kalibrasyon hatası ◆ | average gap between confidence and observed accuracy across bins; always say whether you binned on the top label |
| F1 score / macro-F1 | F1 skoru / makro-F1 ◆ | harmonic mean of precision and recall; *macro* averages over classes, so a rare class counts as much as a common one |
| FLOP | FLOP ◆ | one floating-point operation; the unit training compute is counted in |
| inference | çıkarım | |
| intrinsic / extrinsic evaluation | içsel / dışsal değerlendirme | benchmark vs. downstream task |
| latency | gecikme | |
| Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) | Matthews korelasyon katsayısı ◆ | a balanced single number for a confusion matrix; gives every degenerate baseline (always predicting one class, say) exactly 0 |
| model FLOPs utilization (MFU) | model FLOP kullanımı ◆ | share of a chip's peak throughput a real run actually achieves |
| precision | kesinlik ◆ | of the items the model flagged, the share it got right; *precision* dominant in running text, glossed once per chapter |
| prefill / decode | prefill / decode ◆ | the two halves of a request: the prompt is read in parallel, then output tokens are produced one at a time. Different costs, different bottlenecks |
| prompt caching | prompt önbellekleme | reusing the KV cache of a prompt prefix across requests, so a repeated system prompt is not recomputed |
| quantization | nicemleme | |
| recall | duyarlılık ◆ | of the items it should have flagged, the share it actually found; *recall* dominant in running text, glossed once per chapter |
| ROC curve / AUC | ROC eğrisi / AUC ◆ | recall against false-positive rate; on an imbalanced corpus it looks flattering because the denominator is the large class |
| service level objective (SLO) | hizmet düzeyi hedefi | the latency or availability target a system is held to, stated as a percentile rather than a mean |
| span | span ◆ | one timed unit of work in a trace; *aralık* would be *interval*, a different thing |
| speculative decoding | spekülatif kod çözme ◆ | a small draft model proposes several tokens and the large model verifies them in one pass; same output distribution, fewer serial steps |
| throughput | işlem hacmi / verimlilik | |
| time to first token (TTFT) | ilk token'a kadar geçen süre (TTFT) ◆ | how long the reader waits before anything appears — queueing, prefill and the first decode step; prefill often dominates on long prompts, and it is the number streaming is meant to improve |
| tracing | izleme | recording each step of a request as a linked tree of spans |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Language modelling

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| backoff | geri çekilme | when a long context has no counts, fall back to a shorter one |
| chain rule (of probability) | zincir kuralı | rewrites the probability of a sentence as a product of next-word probabilities; exact, not an approximation |
| held-out data | ayrılmış veri | text the model never trained on; the only honest place to measure |
| interpolation | interpolasyon | mix estimates from several context lengths using fitted weights |
| Markov assumption | Markov varsayımı | only the last n−1 words matter; false, but it makes counting possible |
| maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) | en çok olabilirlik kestirimi | the parameter values that make the observed data most probable; for a categorical distribution that works out to the raw count ratio, which gives probability zero to anything unseen |
| perplexity | perplexity ◆ | how many words the model is effectively choosing between at each step |
| smoothing | düzleştirme | move probability mass onto unseen events so nothing is impossible |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Machine translation

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| back-translation | geri çeviri | translate monolingual target text back into the source to manufacture training pairs; the resource that exists when parallel data does not |
| beam search | ışın araması | keep the k best partial outputs at each step; standard in translation, and actively harmful in open-ended generation |
| BLEU | BLEU ◆ | word n-gram precision against a reference, with a brevity penalty; harsher on morphologically rich languages for a measurable reason |
| chrF | chrF ◆ | the same idea at the character level, which gives partial credit for a word whose stem is right and whose suffix is wrong |
| COMET | COMET ◆ | a learned metric: a model trained to predict human judgements, so it inherits whatever the training data contained |
| translate-test | çeviri ile test | translate incoming text into the model's language at inference; cheap to build, and every translation error is now a model error |
| translate-train | çeviri ile eğitim | translate training data into the target language and train there; pays the translation cost once instead of per request |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Modelling, training, and statistics

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ablation | ablasyon ◆ | remove one component to measure what it was contributing |
| adapter | adaptör | a small trainable module added to a frozen model; LoRA is the form that won |
| alignment | hizalama | making a model behave the way people asked for, rather than the way its training text happened to |
| annealing | tavlama | decaying the learning rate to zero at the end of a run, usually on better data |
| baseline | taban model | the simple model a complex one has to beat to be worth its cost |
| catastrophic forgetting | yıkıcı unutma | *felaket unutması* also seen; training on a new task degrades tasks the model already handled, because the same weights held both |
| continued pretraining | sürdürülen ön eğitim | more of the pretraining objective on new text; adds knowledge and vocabulary, not the ability to follow an instruction |
| cross-validation | çapraz doğrulama | rotate which slice is held out, then average the scores |
| curse of dimensionality | boyut laneti | |
| design matrix | tasarım matrisi | the document-term matrix is one |
| direct preference optimization (DPO) | doğrudan tercih optimizasyonu ◆ | *DPO* dominant; trains on preference pairs directly, with no reward model and no reinforcement-learning loop |
| epoch | devir ◆ | one full pass over the training data; *epok* also seen |
| feature | öznitelik | *değişken* is *variable*, a different thing; *feature engineering* → öznitelik mühendisliği |
| fine-tuning | ince ayar | |
| gradient descent | gradyan inişi | |
| HDBSCAN | HDBSCAN ◆ | finds clusters as regions denser than their surroundings and labels the rest noise; needs no k |
| hyperparameter | hiperparametre | a setting you choose rather than learn; tune on dev, never on test |
| isotonic regression | izotonik regresyon | a non-parametric monotone calibration map fitted by the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm (PAVA); needs roughly a thousand held-out points |
| k-means | k-ortalamalar | partitions points into k groups around their centres; assumes spherical, similarly sized clusters and assigns every point |
| knowledge distillation | bilgi damıtma | training a small model on a large one's outputs; it can inherit fluency, but not correctness the large model never had |
| LoRA (low-rank adaptation) | düşük ranklı uyarlama ◆ | *LoRA* dominant; freezes the pretrained weights and trains a small pair of matrices beside them |
| loss function | kayıp fonksiyonu | |
| overfitting | aşırı öğrenme / aşırı uyum | |
| oversampling / undersampling | aşırı örnekleme / eksik örnekleme | duplicating minority rows, or discarding majority rows, to force a training set into balance |
| parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) | parametre-verimli ince ayar | the family LoRA belongs to: train a small fraction of the weights, leave the rest frozen |
| Platt scaling | Platt ölçeklemesi ◆ | fits a two-parameter sigmoid to a model's raw scores on held-out data; the small-sample calibration default |
| preference pair | tercih çifti | one prompt, two answers, and a judgement of which is better; easier to collect than a correct answer |
| pretraining | ön eğitim | |
| regularization | düzenlileştirme | |
| reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) | insan geri bildiriminden pekiştirmeli öğrenme ◆ | *RLHF* dominant; fits a reward model to human comparisons and then optimizes against it |
| reward model | ödül modeli | a model trained to score answers, standing in for the people whose judgements it was fit to |
| silhouette | siluet ◆ | how much closer a point is to its own cluster than to the next-nearest, on a scale from -1 to 1 |
| supervised fine-tuning (SFT) | denetimli ince ayar | one prompt, one target answer, ordinary next-token loss; the stage that turns a base model into one that answers |
| temperature scaling | sıcaklık ölçeklemesi | divides the logits by one fitted constant T; T > 1 softens the distribution and T < 1 sharpens it, and neither ever changes the ranking |
| verifiable reward | doğrulanabilir ödül | a training signal computed by checking the answer automatically rather than asking a human; only available where correctness is cheap to check |
| verifier | doğrulayıcı | a model trained to score candidate solutions rather than produce them; outcome-supervised ones judge the final answer, process-supervised ones judge each step |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Models and architecture

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| attention | dikkat (mekanizması) | |
| base model | temel model | what pretraining produces: continues text, does not yet answer |
| causal mask | nedensel maske | blocks every position from attending to later ones, so the model can be trained to generate left to right |
| context window | bağlam penceresi | |
| feed-forward network (FFN) | ileri beslemeli ağ | the per-token sublayer of a transformer block; about two thirds of a block's parameters at the usual d_ff = 4d, less in other designs |
| KV cache | KV önbelleği ◆ | stored keys and values from earlier tokens, so generation does not recompute them |
| language model | dil modeli | |
| large language model (LLM) | büyük dil modeli (BDM) | ◆ *LLM* dominant |
| layer normalization | katman normalleştirmesi | rescales one token's own features; not computed across the batch |
| mixture of experts (MoE) | uzman karışımı ◆ | *MoE* dominant; memory follows total parameters and latency follows active ones |
| multi-head attention | çok başlı dikkat | several attention patterns computed in parallel; at a fixed total hidden size each head is narrower, so the cost is close to that of one wide head |
| open-weights model | açık ağırlıklı model | weights downloadable; training data, code and licence are separate questions |
| positional encoding | konumsal kodlama | the position signal added to (or applied to) token embeddings, because attention alone is order-blind |
| residual connection | artık bağlantı | *atlama bağlantısı* also seen; the shortcut that lets a sublayer learn a correction rather than a replacement |
| self-attention | öz-dikkat | |
| transformer | dönüştürücü ◆ | usually left as *Transformer* |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Multimodal

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| contrastive pretraining | karşıtsal ön eğitim | training image and text encoders so matching pairs land close and mismatched pairs land apart; the captions are the supervision |
| optical character recognition (OCR) | optik karakter tanıma | turning an image of text into text; a dedicated engine tends to fail visibly and a VLM fluently, which is a difference of degree since OCR engines use language models too |
| patch embedding | yama gömmesi | an image cut into fixed squares, each projected to the model's hidden size, so a picture becomes a sequence a transformer can read |
| vision-language model (VLM) | görme-dil modeli | a language model with a vision encoder attached, so images and text share one sequence; reads pages, charts and photographs |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Prompting and generation

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| chain-of-thought | düşünce zinciri | |
| chat template | sohbet şablonu | the special tokens that mark who is speaking; fine-tuning with the wrong one trains a format the server will never send |
| faithfulness (of reasoning) | akıl yürütme sadakati | how well a model's stated reasoning matches the process that actually produced its answer; separate from whether either is correct |
| hallucination | halüsinasyon / uydurma | |
| in-context learning | bağlam içi öğrenme | learning a task from examples placed in the prompt; no weight is updated and nothing survives the call |
| instruction tuning | talimat ayarı | fine-tuning on instruction-and-answer pairs so the model answers requests instead of continuing them |
| prompt | istem ◆ | *prompt* dominant in practice |
| temperature | sıcaklık | |
| thinking budget | düşünme bütçesi | a cap on tokens spent inside the reasoning block; hitting it does not cancel the request, it forces an answer out of an unfinished trace |
| verbalised confidence | sözel güven | a 0-100 number the model writes out as text rather than a probability read off its scores; it can be right on average and still separate nothing |
| zero-shot classification | sıfır atışlı sınıflandırma | labelling from an instruction alone, with no examples; a plain completion returns a word rather than a score, so there is no threshold to move unless you also read logprobs or ask for one |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Prompting practice

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| demonstration | örnek gösterim | an input-output pair placed in the prompt; the unit few-shot prompting is built from |
| few-shot | az örnekli | putting a handful of labelled examples in the prompt; *zero-shot* is the no-example case |
| format sensitivity | biçim duyarlılığı | the score changing when the prompt's layout changes but its meaning does not; the reason a single-prompt model comparison is unreliable |
| prompt template | istem şablonu | the fixed scaffolding a prompt is built from, with slots for the input; the thing to version, not the assembled string |

## RAG

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| chunk | parça | the unit you index and retrieve; a modelling decision rather than a preprocessing detail, because it sets what can be retrieved at all |
| grounding | dayandırma | answering from the retrieved text rather than from the model's own memory; separate from whether the retrieval was right |
| lost in the middle | ortada kaybolmak | a model using the beginning and end of a long context better than its middle, so more context is not automatically more information |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

| document-term matrix | belge-terim matrisi | rows = documents, columns = terms |
| dot product | iç çarpım | not *nokta çarpım*; the linear predictor in word2vec |

| latent semantic analysis (LSA) | örtük anlamsal analiz ◆ | *LSA* dominant; PPMI/SVD on counts |

| sparse matrix / sparsity | seyrek matris / seyreklik | |

## Retrieval

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| bi-encoder | çift kodlayıcı | query and document encoded separately, so documents can be indexed ahead of time; the reason dense retrieval scales |
| BM25 | BM25 ◆ | the lexical ranking function every hybrid retriever still has one half of; never translated |
| cross-encoder | çapraz kodlayıcı | query and document read together in one forward pass; far more accurate and impossible to precompute, so it reranks rather than retrieves |
| hard negative | zor negatif | a wrong document that looks right; training on these rather than random ones is most of what makes a dense retriever work |
| recall@k | recall@k ◆ | the share of a query's relevant documents in the top k; with one relevant document per query it reduces to did it appear at all, also called hit rate. The ceiling on what downstream grounding can use |
| reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) | sıra tersine dayalı birleştirme (RRF) ◆ | combine ranked lists by summing 1/(k+rank); a variance-reduction trick for comparable systems, and a way to lose accuracy when they are not |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Sequence labeling and extraction

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| BIO tagging | BIO etiketleme | B marks a span's first token, I its continuation, O everything else; the scheme that turns spans into per-token labels |
| conditional random field (CRF) | conditional random field ◆ | scores a whole label sequence at once by adding a learned transition score for each adjacent label pair; models the labels given the words rather than their joint distribution, which is what lets its features overlap freely |
| entity linking | varlık bağlama | mapping a mention to a canonical id; distinct from recognising that the mention is an entity at all |
| gazetteer | varlık sözlüğü | a memorised list of known entity strings; a strong, dumb baseline and a poor generaliser |
| named entity recognition (NER) | adlandırılmış varlık tanıma ◆ | *NER* dominant in practice; finding and typing mentions of people, organisations and places |
| nested entity | iç içe varlık | a span inside another span; BIO cannot represent it, which is why span-based decoders exist |
| relation extraction | ilişki çıkarma | classifying the relation that holds between two already-identified mentions |
| span-level F1 | span düzeyinde F1 | a prediction counts only if type, start and end all match; the metric token accuracy hides |
| token classification | token sınıflandırma | one label per token; the architecture NER, POS tagging and chunking all share |
| Viterbi decoding | Viterbi kod çözme ◆ | picks the highest-scoring whole label sequence rather than the best label at each position independently |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Summarization and generation

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| abstractive summarization | soyutlayıcı özetleme | the summary is generated, so it can use words the source never used -- and assert facts it never contained |
| coverage / density | kapsam / yoğunluk | how much of a summary is copied from its source, and in how long a stretch; characterises a corpus before any model sees it |
| extractive summarization | çıkarımsal özetleme | the summary is a selection of source sentences, so it cannot invent wording and cannot compress below a sentence; it can still mislead by omitting the context that governs a selected sentence |
| faithfulness (to source) | kaynağa sadakat | whether a summary asserts only what the source supports; separate from whether it reads well, invisible to n-gram overlap, and not the same thing as faithfulness of reasoning |
| lead-3 | lead-3 ◆ | the first three sentences as a summary; a baseline that beats trained models on some corpora and not others -- measure before assuming |
| LLM-as-judge | LLM hakemi | scoring generated text with another model; carries position, length and self-preference biases that must be measured, not assumed away |
| ROUGE | ROUGE ◆ | n-gram overlap against a reference summary; rewards copying, blind to faithfulness, and dependent on a tokenizer that mangles Turkish |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Text, tokens, and morphology

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| agglutinative | eklemeli | Turkish stacks suffixes on a stem; why tokenizers fragment it |
| byte-pair encoding (BPE) | byte-pair encoding ◆ | never translated; *BPE* in running text |
| Common Crawl | Common Crawl ◆ | proper noun, never translated; the monthly web crawl most corpora start from |
| corpus | derlem | plural *derlemler* |
| fertility | fertility ◆ | of a tokenizer: tokens per word. Used to compare tokenizers on the same text, or languages under one tokenizer on matched content — and it is not the bill: languages differ in words per sentence too |
| hapax legomena | hapax legomena ◆ | Latin, kept as-is; words occurring exactly once |
| lemmatization | sözlük biçimine indirgeme | reducing a word to its dictionary form; see *stemming* — the pair is easy to swap |
| n-gram / bigram | n-gram ◆ / ikili n-gram | *n-gram* takes Turkish suffixes: *n-gram'lar* |
| normalization | normalleştirme | the preprocessing ladder; cf. *L2 normalization* |
| stemming | gövdeleme | chopping suffixes by rule; the result need not be a real root or a dictionary form (cf. *lemmatization*) |
| stop word | stop word ◆ | English lists do not transfer to Turkish; *etkisiz kelime* is also seen, but these words are not meaningless — which to drop depends on the task |
| subword | alt kelime | *alt kelime bölütlemesi* = subword tokenization |
| token | token ◆ | left as *token*; *jeton* and *birim* are not used |
| tokenization | bölütleme ◆ | *tokenizasyon* common in practice |
| vocabulary | sözlük | also *dictionary*; disambiguate when both are in play |
| Zipf's law | Zipf yasası | |

: {tbl-colwidths="[35,35,30]"}

## Turkish and morphology

| English | Türkçe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| deasciification | Türkçe karakter geri kazanımı | restoring Turkish diacritics to text typed without them; the alternative -- stripping them everywhere -- merges *oldu* with *öldü*. Not *şapka düzeltme*, which is the circumflex (â, î, û) and a different problem |
| dotted and dotless i | noktalı ve noktasız i | Turkish has two i letters, dotted and dotless, so İ/i and I/ı are two pairs and four case forms; str.lower() maps them wrongly in both directions and emits a combining mark that splits words |
| vowel harmony | ünlü uyumu | the stem's vowels decide which form each suffix takes, which is why one grammatical ending has four or eight spellings |
